values.note: $20 a night, with the fee and registration procedure posted at the campground kiosk. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.

fees.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/emilylake ('Overnight fees ($20 for most sites) and registration procedures are posted at the information kiosk at each campground'; 'A Recreation Passport (park pass) is required for vehicle entry into all state park and forest campgrounds') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (Emily Lake State Forest Campground: 9 sites, $20), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Drinking water from a hand-pump well. Boating access site (ramp) in the campground.

facilities.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/emilylake ('There are vault toilets.' 'Potable (drinking) water is available from a hand-pump well.' 'There's a boating access site in the campground.') + amenity table (boat access: R), read 2026-10-25

booking.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/emilylake ('No reservations. Sites available on a first-come, first-served basis.' 'Camping is limited to a 15-day maximum stay.') + amenity table ('Reservable at MiDNRReservations.com': no), read 2026-10-25

values.note: 'Nine tent and small trailer sites' (the DNR's standard state forest wording; no maximum length posted). One camping unit and six people per site.

sites.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/emilylake ('This rustic campground offers nine tent and small trailer sites'; 'One camping unit and six people are allowed per site') + amenity table (9 campsites), read 2026-10-25

note: Rustic state forest campground on 54-acre Emily Lake (largemouth bass, bluegill, rainbow trout, perch), Houghton County, 3.8 miles south of Twin Lake via M-26 South and Emily Lake Road; sites shaded by conifers and hemlock with lake views. The DNR advises against GPS routing via Pike Lake Road from M-38, which is mostly gravel: take M-38 to M-26 to Emily Lake Road. Near the 41-mile Bill Nicholls Trail. --Claude
summary: DNR page + SF amenity table: 9 sites, $20 at the kiosk + Recreation Passport, no electric, vault toilets, hand-pump water, boat access, first-come only, 15-day max (all confirmed). Access: the DNR routes drivers via M-26 and Emily Lake Road to avoid gravel Pike Lake Road (paved route exists; no 4WD or big-rig warning). Phone missing (flag). Note trimmed of field restatements.
